profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 5 sits at 4489 East Sahara Avenue, Las Vegas, Nevada, directly adjacent to Switch's Las Vegas 4 building, part of an earlier Sahara Avenue-addressed cluster (Las Vegas 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6) distinct from the larger, newer Decatur Boulevard, Capovilla Avenue, and Lindell Road buildings that make up the bulk of Switch's Core Campus square footage. Switch's own current website does not publish individual square footage, megawatt capacity, year-opened, or redundancy-design figures for Las Vegas 5; its address is confirmed only through this record's own OpenStreetMap tagging and corroborating third-party data center aggregator listings, not a dedicated Switch spec page. Switch's Core Campus overall is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy, with newer, larger buildings such as Las Vegas 8, 9, and 10 individually documented in Switch's own press archive while the Sahara Avenue cluster including Las Vegas 5 predates that level of individual public disclosure. Switch's Nevada tax-advantages materials describe a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent and a 75 percent property-tax abatement on customer equipment at Switch facilities, administered through Nevada's Governor's Office of Economic Development, applicable campus-wide rather than to any one building specifically. Switch does not name a specific power utility on its Las Vegas pages, though NV Energy is the incumbent utility across Clark County as a matter of public record.

Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary U.S. data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs, drawing additional colocation and hyperscale investment from other operators over the past decade. The Sahara Avenue cluster including Las Vegas 5 sits closer to the Las Vegas Strip and downtown core than Switch's larger, newer Decatur Boulevard, Capovilla Avenue, and Lindell Road buildings farther southwest in unincorporated Enterprise, reflecting the campus's geographic growth pattern over more than two decades of continuous expansion since Rob Roy's original 2002 founding purchase.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 5 is one building in Switch's Las Vegas Core Campus, a 495-megawatt cluster on the southwest side of Las Vegas that has grown over two decades from a single 2002 purchase into the operator's largest footprint. The building itself sits on East Sahara Avenue adjacent to Las Vegas 4, part of an older cluster of five contiguous buildings distinct from Switch's newer, larger facilities farther southwest in Enterprise. Switch publishes no individual megawatt capacity, square footage, or redundancy rating for Las Vegas 5; the operator markets the entire Core Campus at up to 495 megawatts upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy, with disclosure at the building level reserved for newer facilities.

Las Vegas 5 qualifies under Switch's proprietary Tier 5 Platinum rating, which does not derive from a third-party certification standard. The facility receives power from NV Energy, the Clark County incumbent utility, though Switch does not name a specific power contract on its public pages. Nevada tax law applies a 75 percent property-tax abatement on customer equipment and a consumer-use-tax abatement to as low as 2 percent across the Core Campus, administered through the state's Governor's Office of Economic Development.

Nevada has 26 mapped data center facilities and only 10.37 megawatts of published capacity across all operators. Las Vegas 5 is part of the third-ranked capacity cluster statewide by published megawatts, but contributes no disclosed individual figure to that ranking; the absence of a published megawatt count for this building reflects the operator's practice of aggregating disclosure to the campus level rather than the building level for its older Sahara Avenue cluster.
